name: Claim-Warrant Conformance Suite
description: Reference implementation and adversarial conformance suite accompanying the working paper Consensus Is Not Evidence: Claim-Bounded Adjudication for Automated Settlement (Nsonzi, 2026). The paper specifies a claim-warrant layer between adjudication and payment that enforces one invariant — a claim may assert no more than its evidence, procedure, and scope warrant, Settlement(V) ⇒ V ∈ W(E, P, C). This deposit contains the executable decision-logic models and the constructed cases that demonstrate the layer's logical separation from admissibility-only and consensus-only mechanisms.Contents: • cases.py — the 39 constructed cases (25 defective, 14 warranted), each with its expected decision derived from the declared warrant relation rather than hand-assigned. • gates.py, cws.py — decision-logic for the three gates (admissibility, warrant, settlement sufficiency) and the claim-warrant settlement model, including the signed, versioned capability registry used in the warrant-downgrade case. • run.py — the harness; running it regenerates every reported figure. • case-catalogue.md, results-matrix.md, conformance-results.md — generated case listing and result tables. • rails-vs-settlement-layer.md — the division-of-labour comparison.
